title: shit that makes no sense
content:
shit that makes no sense
when you look back at the best of years of your life, they’re actually the ones where you were climbing out of hell...shattered, emerging from catastrophic loss, covered in blood and shards of broken glass
laughable prima facie yet strangely well-supported in psychology/philosophy -- ie the freudism “in hindsight the years of struggle will strike you as the most beautiful”
2/4
if I had to try and put words to it - shit just fills you with the energy that anything is possible, and that with the grace of God you can literally destroy and rebuild yourself at will. a man moves entirely different once this is understood
the residue of failure ends up engendering such, like, nonsensically-powerful strength in you - "the peace of God which passeth all understanding" - that it’s not so much you look forward to fucking up…but that when it inevitably happens, you feel it, it sucks, and then you shake it off as some newly-acquired bell in your head starts ringing. "This is gonna be good for you -- because it ALWAYS IS.”
3/4
I tell people all the time now when things arent going their way -
“YOU HAVEN’T SUFFERED ENOUGH TO GET WHAT YOU WANT.”
most of them look at me crazy. and I mean, theyre not wrong...one, I am, and two, that's some wild-ass shit to say to someone who is up against it lol
but some ppl, they just silently nod their head...been thru enough life to understand...and come right back w/ some variation of "you're dead right...lets go fucking get some."
4/4
final "makes no sense" is that you learn to flip the script
DO NOT TRUST SUCCESS
never ever ever. always give that mf the side-eye.
if you’ve traded markets long enough I shouldnt even have to tell you, bc you already know...nothing breeds failure like success.
stokes pride, ego, vanity, all the demons, all the leading indicators of your next crashout
hence why trollope wrote "success is a poison that should only be taken late in life, and then only in small doses"...or seneca who has 1000 maxims, barbs and jeremiads on the perils of success, that "he who lays on a perfumed couch is no less dead than he who is dragged by the executioner's hook."
things never change, human nature never changes. the sages & philosophers, they've been saying for 2000 years what I'm about to say
you can trust pain. it might actually be the only thing you can trust; I'm not there yet, but I'm also not far from it.
so if you're fucked up bad and not sure how you'll ever get out of it...you need blind faith in two things. one, that all greatness comes from suffering, from the lows and from chaos. two, that at the time when you desperately need it the most, God will grant you strength.
just as Malamud wrote, "There comes a time in a man's life, when to get where he has to go - if there are no doors or windows - he walks through a wall."
that's exactly how it goes. pain turns you to a beast...trust, believe, and keep it pushing.

title: China is implementing export licenses on silver st...
content:
China is implementing export licenses on silver starting January 1st essentially restricting which companies can ship it internationally. 
This is a big deal because China supplies roughly 60-70% of globally traded silver and most exporters won't qualify for the new licenses. 
The market's already pricing this in, with Shanghai silver jumping to $85/oz and creating a $5 premium over US prices.​​
Silver has surged 175% in 2025 because it's become critical infrastructure that most people don't realize. 
Every solar panel needs silver paste to capture sunlight, the entire renewable energy buildout depends on it. 
EVs require 2-3 times more silver than gas cars due to battery management systems and charging infrastructure.
 AI data centers are silver intensive machines with far more conductive connections than traditional servers and with 33% of new computing capacity being dedicated to AI, that's enormous structural demand. 
Semiconductors, 5G equipment, medical devices and water filtration systems all require silver with no viable substitutes.​​
The problem is that 70% of silver is produced as a byproduct of copper, lead, and zinc mining. 
You can't just "make more silver", you only get it when those other metals are mined. 
Mine production rose just 0.9% in 2024 despite surging prices and demand, creating persistent deficits exceeding 200 million ounces in 2025. 
Recycling can't close the gap.​
China's licensing requirement is a geopolitical play securing domestic supply for their solar manufacturers while creating global scarcity that benefits their state approved exporters. 
Combined with structural supply deficits that can't be solved quickly, silver is becoming a genuine industrial bottleneck for the entire clean energy and AI infrastructure transition. 
This shortage will likely stay in place for years.
BREAKING: China will be imposing export restrictions on silver beginning in 5 days, on January 1st.
These restrictions will require special government licenses for silver exports.
Shanghai silver prices are now up to $85/oz, a ~$5 premium to spot prices in the US. https://t.co/Dw2R3ytaAv

title: everything is driven by two motives, a selfless on...
content:
everything is driven by two motives, a selfless one and a selfish one. 
understanding this truth, esp the selfish side, is the best way to consistently do the "right" thing & understand all human nature.
Plato's Tripartite Theory of the Soul - the Chariot with two horses...that image applies for selfish and selfless motives. 
”Man and his symbols,” wrote Jung, shaking his head… 
--
THREE EXAMPLES:
1. anger -- forget if its right or wrong, forget the selfless motive for now.
anger only gets in YOUR way. it clouds your mind, it leads to decisions driven by passion/emotion instead of reason
the sages & philosophers (thinking Cicero, Peripatetics) agree that an angry man is actually the closest thing to insanity - he legit changes color, his voice changes, totally irrational in speech and becomes, temporarily, a "crazy person." 
the selfish motive is more convincing than the selfless motive.
2. forgiveness. the hardest thing on earth. 
forget right or wrong, forget selfless... you not being able to forgive, again, clouds your mind. grudges, grievances, these only hold you back in life. they turn you bitter and resentful and focused on the past instead of the future.
the selfish motive, again, is the more powerful one. 
"you should do this because its right" rarely works on people..."you should do this because you're only holding yourself back" will make a man examine his behavior.
3. all hatred/cruelty/prejudice. 
forget selfless. selfish: you are not viewing the world objectively, stuck in a cage of preconceived notions and biases...just not seeing the true nature of things at all. 
we dont even have to talk about the "wrong" side of it - you're fully irrational.
but more than anything, a hateful heart weighs you down. you will never know peace until you fix this defect of character, forgive, remove anger, and re-wire yourself.
"do it because its right," no one responds to that, and if they do, its never permanent. 
"do it because you are fucking your own life up" - that resonates and it can lead to permanent change.
--
removing anger, learning to forgive, letting light into a hateful heart, these are not overnight fixes.
just as the bio quote says: sculptor and marble. it takes years, you don’t get to just whack off defective chunks of character overnight. God didn't plan it that way.
recognize that God, nature, deus sive natura, are perfect in all things. 
think of muscle growth. it takes time to build, and you get frustrated with how long it takes
but then once you have it, you realize it stays on - thats exactly why it took so long...you wouldn't want it on/off overnight. the creator is perfect in all ways
same goes for behavior - you dont want on/off - you want it to get gone, and stay gone. and so that takes time...perfect in all ways.
as far as changes in behavior - bad habits never fully leave, but your discipline becomes stronger than your desire. urges and desires pop up like that gopher game, and the speed at which you whack them back down becomes damn-near instantaneous; "nah, we aint doing that." 
the speed is the change. anger can never be fully removed, nothing can...don't ever expect that. emotions are hardwired. but your response and speed, you can marble/sculpt the hell out of that with consistent daily effort.
that's the reality of change.
--
what is the main takeaway from this?
stop worrying about what everyone else is doing. 
the "crowd" is driven by those things I just mentioned: anger, cruelty and prejudice. Twitter is fueled by these things and is just a cesspool of hate.
none of that is your business
you cant save everybody. you can only save yourself. 
the best start is thru embracing these selfish motives with a critical eye, one that is indifferent to the world...and then day by day, chip away at your flaws in private.
as you do this, you will find that two things occur simultaneously:
1. your distance from the crowd will naturally increa[...]

title: every man you will ever meet is a pile of virtues ...
content:
every man you will ever meet is a pile of virtues and vices 
none are good or bad.
some are more good than bad. others are more bad than good.
that's as wide as the range of outcomes goes
to go beyond that (as most ppl do) is wrong in the Noble Eightfold Path sense: Wrong View/Wrong Thought. 
2/7
you got the wrong goggles, the wrong glasses on, and its going to trip you up.
all good men have reprehensible faults. all bad men have redeeming qualities.
a man is a pile of virtues and a pile of vices - period.
some got more on one side, some got more on the other, but everyone's got a big pile of both.
to view reality thru any other lens than this one represents some sort of sickness, cruelty or prejudice...a hateful heart...but undeniably, Wrong View.
3/7
think of people you know. God scatters those virtues and vices around. no one has all of them, on either side...and people will always surprise you in both directions.
so that's what I mean by, you've got some dark-ass tint on your glasses that is distorting your view of the world. 
you don't see the good pile in people.
I don't care abt you being right/wrong, its more dire than that -- you're walking around impaired.
4/7 
a great meme is the one where the guy winces and it says:
"...when the worst person you know just made a valid point."
that's what life is like with fucked up glasses. Wrong View. Wrong Thought.
Reality is not contorting to your preconceived, fixed, rigid view of the world, driven by emotion and bias. That will cause you unrelenting pain. 
But reality isn't wrong... reality is reality. You're the one who wakes up and chooses hate.
people who live life that way are tortured every day...TORTURED.
5/7 
good ppl are gonna do bad things. bad ppl are gonna do good things. pile of virtues, pile of vices. 
its the hateful side you see more...people literally destroying their own lives each day, mental gymnastics on some Dhalsim shit. 
legitimate mental self-mutilation. zero sympathy for ya...God punishes a hateful heart by ensuring they never know a moment of peace.
trump is the live case study - hes got some good and some bad. but the "he's 100% bad w/ no good" crowd...every day is hell when you live like that. because no one is 100% bad.
the other side (100% good) is wrong too, but good is good. no war has ever been waged as a result of both sides looking for the good in one another.
being consumed by hate 24/7 destroys you
6/7
you just gotta give people their due. I say all the time "I don't like the guy, but he's right." thats all you gotta do, man...all you gotta do.
I dont care if he's Pol Pot - if you cant call balls and strikes as you see them, if you cant describe an action for what it is without bias, emotion or prejudice...well, what are you as a man?
unbiased, unemotional - pick 3 descriptors for the action.
i'd go with spineless, cowardly, and weak-minded.
a strong mind easily separates man vs action, message vs messenger.
a weak-mind is incarcerated. it can't escape itself, its flooded with hatred and prejudice...all the fuckin circuits are shot, there is no rational brain function, no reason, no logic, no emotional self-discipline. just error and blind fury. 
very sad - as Pascal wrote, there is a God-shaped vacuum in each man that can only be filled by the creator...that's the only thing that can save a hateful heart.
7/7
where it gets real tricky, and I think/write about this a ton...is that every man's virtues and vices are intertwined.
its all connected, you cannot disentangle a virtue or a vice from someone.
hence the saying "your greatest weakness is often your greatest strength taken too far."
alternatively, "the greater the sinner, the greater the saint."
this is the duality of man.
its also why I dont bet against people...I've learned that any man of strong will and powerful passions, like, those are equidistant.
some men dont do shit, some men do a lot of shi[...]

For the first time in over a decade, there are now 530,000 more home sellers than buyers, the biggest gap ever recorded. 
This should be great news for young people trying to buy homes, but it's exposing a political problem.
Trump openly admitted that helping young buyers requires driving prices down, which tanks the wealth of existing homeowners, mostly boomers.​
Young people have basically stopped buying homes.
 
84%  of Gen Z is delaying homeownership because prices are still astronomical despite this massive inventory glut. 
The median first time buyer is now 40 years old. 
You need to earn $141,000 just to afford a median priced home when the average salary is $75,000. 
Even with sellers desperate to offload properties, the core problem remains, homes cost way too much because mortgage rates are above 6% (up from pandemic lows of 3%), and boomer homeowners have seen their properties appreciate by 33% in five years.​
This creates a dilemma for Trump because increase housing supply to lower prices and help young buyers, or protect the wealth boomers built through home appreciation. 
Trump said it himself, he wants to "keep up" boomer home values while making it possible for young people to buy. 
You can't do both.

title: Heavy truck sales are a leading indicator of the l...
content:
Heavy truck sales are a leading indicator of the labor market because they reveal what businesses actually believe about the future. 
When trucking companies and logistics operators are optimistic, they buy trucks, it's a capital investment that signals confidence in handling more volume. 
When they're uncertain, truck purchases are one of the first expenses they cut. 
It's a direct window into business sentiment that often shows up in employment decisions months later.
Truck sales have dropped to 5.1 million units over the last 12 months, the lowest since 2020, and outside the pandemic period, you'd have to go back eight years to find this weakness. 
The decline of roughly 1.1 million units over the past 18 months represents a meaningful shift in how business leaders are thinking about demand and capacity.
The historical relationship is consistent and notable, virtually every time truck sales have peaked and declined in past economic cycles, unemployment has risen roughly six months later. 
If this pattern holds, the unemployment rate could rise by at least one percentage point over the next six months. 
For context, if unemployment is currently around 4%, that would push it toward 5%, a noticeable shift that signals the labor market is beginning to cool and business confidence is declining.
The US unemployment rate is likely heading higher:
US heavy truck sales are down to 5.1 million over the last 12 months, the lowest since 2020.
Outside the pandemic, this is the lowest level in 8 years.
Annual truck sales have declined by ~1.1 million over the last 18 months.
In previous economic cycles, this has been a leading indicator of higher unemployment.
This suggests that the unemployment rate may rise by at least 1.0 percentage point over the next 6 months.
Downside pressure on the labor market is building. 
- 
The Kobeissi Letter
